tagline: Across the rice country to the shrimp boats at Delcambre.
intro: Highway 14 runs 34 miles across Vermilion Parish from Gueydan to Delcambre, over gently sloping land with allées of shade trees and cheniers, coastal ridges grown up in oak. The drained marshes are rice fields that double as crawfish ponds, and cattle graze near the marsh edge. Many people here speak French, as their ancestors did.

It was hunting country first. In the 1860s Jean Pierre Gueydan came out from Abbeville after deer, ducks and geese, then gave land to bring a Southern Pacific branch line in for the rice farmers. The first irrigation pump in Louisiana went in nearby, at Primeaux Landing.

moments.title: Kaplan
moments.text: Most of the first settlers were Acadian and spoke French, and on July 14, 1906, the young town held its first Bastille Day celebration.

moments.title: Abbeville
moments.text: Père Mégret named the town in 1844 for his birthplace in France, and the C.S. Steen mill here has made pure cane syrup for close to a hundred years.

moments.title: Delcambre
moments.text: A shrimping town on the Vermilion and Iberia parish line, where the shrimp boats and their nets are on view and the shrimp get a festival of their own.
